approval_doc_subject: Test pressing approval against the digital master
approval_subtitle: Report of {date} · measured against the digital master of each side, using the latest recording of each copy
measurement_text: Recordings on the station's turntable; turntable speed from the calibration subtracted
overview_note: Speed: cut and pressing against the master (median). Center hole: median. Copies: grade against the master, median. Pre-echo: strongest, relative to the music. Clicks/min: real clicks per minute of music, median.
how_to_read: How to read this: whatever sits at the same spot on all copies is in the stamper or the cut and affects the whole run. Whatever only one copy has (dust, static, pressing flaws) affects only that copy. A few audible stamper defects are a note for the pressing plant, not a reason to withhold approval.
copies_note: Clicks and pops per minute of music that the master does not explain; loud: strength {audible} or more. Speed: cut and pressing against the master, turntable subtracted. Treble: 10 kHz at the end of the side relative to the start.
audible_on_several: Audible defects on several copies (stamper / cut)
timeline_note: Tracks at the top. Row “Stamper”: spots that sit at the same place (±3 ms) on at least two copies; the audible ones bold and labeled. Below, each copy's real clicks (on the vinyl only, according to the master); size by strength, outlined: audible.
spectrogram_copy: Spectrogram of {copy} with the stamper defects
spectrogram_note: Time axis of the recording. Lines: audible defects at the same spot on several copies.
zooms_title: Audible stamper defects close up, per copy (±{s} s)
zooms_note: The triangles mark the spot. A click in the stamper shows up on every copy as the same thin vertical line right there.
charts_title: Frequency response, wow, level per track
charts_note: Frequency response: median of the copies for each third of the side (start, middle, end), relative to 1 kHz, groove noise subtracted; includes cartridge and phono preamp. Wow: speed variation per revolution at the start, middle and end of the side. Level: per track against the master, relative to the median.
method_text: Each copy is recorded on the station's turntable and laid against the digital master of the side sample by sample: time axis (speed and wow), polarity, channels, frequency response, level per track and gaps. Every detection of the click detector is checked against the master: whatever remains after subtracting the master is a real click on the vinyl, the rest is music. Defects that sit at the same spot (±3 ms) on several copies come from the stamper or the cut; by chance there would be very few.
crit_treble: Treble at the end of the side (10 kHz)
thresholds_note: A single bad copy does not speak against the run. Audible here means: strength {audible} or more (provisional, calibrated against a mastering engineer's judgment of real test pressings). The thresholds are suggestions and can be changed.
kpi_clicks_quiet_net: Clicks/min in quiet passages above floor
kpi_ticks_quiet_net: Crackle/min in quiet passages above floor
clicks_note: Detections per time slice; below the axis the lead-in and run-out (not counted).
role_secondary: quiet passages, one step at most
top_events_note: NN: click probability of the grooveclean neural network. real?: probability according to the learned model (master comparisons and judgments) that the detection is a real click and not music.
scale_note: The grade is a suggestion derived from the measurements; the limits are starting values and not yet calibrated by ear on many records. Clicks and pops in the music decide; quiet passages lower the grade by one step at most; F only for a backward skip.
